requirements.requirement: Every command run through sudo on node1 is logged to /var/log/sudo-commands.log
requirements.summary: A sudoers drop-in (/etc/sudoers.d/sudo-command-logging) sets logfile=/var/log/sudo-commands.log; entries were shown appearing in that file for multiple sudo invocations by both root and a disposable test user (testsudo), and again after a reboot, confirming the mechanism logs every sudo command.

requirements.requirement: Logged entries include the invoking user and a timestamp
requirements.summary: log_year and log_host directives were added and the captured log lines show a full date/time, the invoking user before the colon (e.g. 'root :' and 'testsudo :'), host, and the executed command, for both root and the temporary testsudo user.

requirements.requirement: Sudo log entries are kept out of the general system log (syslog/authpriv/journald)
requirements.summary: The '!syslog' directive disables sudo's default syslog output; grep against /var/log/secure and journalctl for the same commands returned zero matches both before and after the reboot, directly confirming exclusion from the general system log.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: pre-restart healthy state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered config/log/exclusion behavior
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline boot_id, sudoers validity, and log file state were captured (cmd-20cb5c3d3af44942, matching global before_prepare boot-identity f43afa1c...). A backgrounded 'systemctl reboot' returned an acknowledgement (pid) before the node dropped (cmd-431c58df14fc48e5), the node became briefly unreachable (cmd-c036851be08f480e) then returned with a distinct boot_id (cmd-bd7e494b452e4aa0, matching global after_executor boot-identity 8c353e7c...). Post-reboot checks confirmed sudoers still validates, the log file/permissions persisted, a new sudo command was captured, and it was still absent from journald (cmd-5eee06283412426f).

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct evidence: sudo commands are logged to /var/log/sudo-commands.log with user and timestamp via a validated sudoers drop-in, and '!syslog' confirmed excludes these entries from /var/log/secure and journald both before and after a reboot. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also executed cleanly, with baseline and post-reboot boot identities, an acknowledged reboot, and confirmed recovery of the logging configuration and log file. Minor hygiene deduction for two small leftover files in /tmp.
limitations: The post-reboot verification command (cmd-5eee06283412426f) had an overall non-zero exit code, but this is explained by 'grep -c' returning 1 on zero matches (the expected/desired outcome), not a functional failure.

Log content interpretation relies on the standard sudo log format (invoking_user : HOST=... ; USER=runas_user ; COMMAND=...); this was not independently cross-verified against sudo documentation in the evidence, though it is consistent across all shown entries.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands were purposeful and reverted where temporary (the testsudo verification user was created in cmd-a9f883b8878b4766 and fully removed in cmd-a56c1a1d93bf4b9b/cmd-61031fd7de2b4815 after a first userdel attempt failed on a lingering session). Minor unnecessary residue remains: the staging file /tmp/sudo-command-logging (created in cmd-bdb41f8a9b6f43f9) and /tmp/reboot.log (produced by the backgrounded reboot in cmd-431c58df14fc48e5) were left in /tmp after task completion, visible in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot. These are low-risk, non-sensitive leftovers with no security or functional impact, but represent unremoved scratch artifacts.
